summary: Colville National Forest summit in Pend Oreille County, WA: a 1930 10-ft L-4 cab tower, out of use by the 1950s, fallen by 1960; remains reported on the summit, access unstated.

facts.status_note: Tower gone: the cab was removed or destroyed in the 1950s (sources differ), the tower had fallen by 1960, and the house was razed by 1964; the register says remains can still be found on the summit

access.note: Colville National Forest land per FFLOS; no source states current public access to the summit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb all give 1930 for the 10-foot L-4 cab tower, but the June 1931 newspaper item describes a lookout station being built when the lightning strike happened. The story reports the 1930 date and the 1931 account side by side and does not reconcile them.

The register says the cab was removed in the 1950s; Firelookout.com says destroyed in the 1950s. WillhiteWeb gives the later fallen-tower and razed-house dates (1960, 1964). The story gives both 1950s versions.

WillhiteWeb calls the 1931 injured man the watchman, but the same page and the 1931 newspaper item say he was a carpenter employed by the Forest Service. The story uses the carpenter role and leaves out the watchman label and the man's name.

sources.title: Hall Mountain Lookout Site (above Sullivan Lake)

notes_for_editor: Four pages, two of them short. The 1931 newspaper item names a private individual; the story and this record leave the name and age out. Firelookout.com credits its photos to the Dave Bula collection and the Fire Lookout Museum, and the FFLOS page has a Photos section; neither was fetched and no licence is known, so no photo is listed. No source describes the summit today or says whether it is open to the public. The 1933 'new' tower may or may not be the 1930 one. The access route WillhiteWeb describes (Sullivan Creek Road trailhead) is not stated as current and is left out of the story.
